introduction.summary: A rotor assembly is the complete rotating part of a machine — here a multistage pump rotor: shaft, impellers, interstage sleeves, balance drum, thrust collar, locknuts and coupling hub. balance.title: Two-plane balancing
balance.description: The rotor is spun on the balancing machine; sensors measure the vibration at each support. Correction weights are removed or added in two planes (yellow) so that both static and couple unbalance (red) are within the ISO 21940-11 grade (e.g. G2.5).

video_tutorials.title: Rotor Assembly — Introduction

script.narration: This module introduces the Rotor Assembly.
A rotor assembly is the complete rotating element of a machine.
For a multistage pump it includes the shaft, impellers, interstage sleeves, balance drum, thrust collar, locknuts and coupling hub, assembled in sequence and then dynamically balanced in two planes.
Typical applications include pump and compressor overhauls; motor and turbine rotors; spare (ready-to-install) rotors; balancing shop work.
The cutaway reveals the internal construction: Shaft (stepped, ground journals), Impeller Stage 1 (keyed), Interstage Sleeve 1, Impeller Stage 2 (keyed).
The exploded view separates every component so each one can be tapped for its function, material and failure modes.
Next, watch the operation tutorial to see how it works.

script.narration: How the Rotor Assembly works.
The shaft is checked for straightness (run-out).
Impellers and sleeves are fitted in sequence, keyed and locked.
The balance drum and thrust collar complete the stack; locknuts lock it.
On the balancing machine the rotor is spun and unbalance is measured at both supports.
Correction in two planes brings the residual unbalance within the grade.

video_tutorials.title: Rotor Assembly — Maintenance

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Rotor Assembly.
Store spare rotor protected; rotate periodically if horizontal.
Check run-out before installation.
Re-balance after any component change.
Watch for high vibration after overhaul: 1× vibration. Common cause: imbalance, bent shaft, loose fits.
Watch for axial rub: noise, wear. Common cause: wrong stack-up/impeller positions.
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.
